- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and news volume is high, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) and prices are rising, model often fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to correct.
- After a sharp price spike (≥3% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above prior peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume drops to 0–1, model underreacts; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to compensate for lag.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 period windows; if forecast is >2% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0%.
- When sentiment is flat (0.33–0.67) and news volume is low, model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to avoid underreaction.
